summary: Deborah Klimburg-Salter is a scholar of Tibetology and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD under Oleg Grabar at Harvard and completed her Habilitation at the University of Vienna, where she held the chair of Asian art history from 1994 to 2015.
Declan Quigley is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He has taught at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

Dedong Wei is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Renmin University of China around 1995–1998, where he became an associate professor of religious studies around 1998.
Demchok Dorje studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

Denis Sinor was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar, linguist, and historian. He studied under Paul Pelliot and at the University of Cambridge, where he later worked (1948–1962) before serving as a director at Indiana University Bloomington (1962–1986).

Denis Twitchett was a Sinologist and historian who studied at SOAS and St Catharine's College. He held the Chair of Chinese at the University of London (1960–1968) and Cambridge (1968–1980), and was later emeritus at Princeton University (1980–1994).

Denise Bernot was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the École des chartes and the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes. She held a post at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from circa 1960 to 1989.

Denma Lochö Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery and Gyume Tantric College under various traditional teachers, was a research fellow at Calcutta University, principal of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and abbot of Namgyal Monastery.
Dennis A. Johnson is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes, attested in 2012.

Dennis Hirota is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley and earned his PhD from Nagoya University. He served as a professor in the Faculty of Letters at Ryukoku University around 1996 and was a visiting professor at Harvard Divinity School in 2008.
Dennis Hudson was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who taught in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies at Smith College, attested between 1987 and 2000.

Denzaburo Yoshizawa was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji. He held academic posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University (circa 1954–1988) and Iryo Sosei University.

Derek F. Maher is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his MA and PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He has lectured at Virginia and UNC Greensboro, and co-directed the Religious Studies Program at East Carolina University.

Dermot Killingley is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Oxford and SOAS. He taught at the University of Malaya (1961–1968) and served as Reader at Newcastle University (1970–2000).

Dermott Joseph Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (BA) and Leiden University (MA) before earning his PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles in 2018 under William M. Bodiford.

Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar was an Indologist and historian. He served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (attested 1910) and Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of India's Western Circle (1911–1917).
Dewei Zhang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under the doctoral supervision of Jinhua Chen, attested in 2010.
Dezhung Kunga Gyaltsen studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Gaton Ngawang Lekpa, Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, and Ngawang Nyima, and participated in a research project at the University of Washington from 1960 to 1972.

Dhammanandā is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007) under Tilak Kariyawasam and Daya Edirisinghe, having also studied under Viên Minh, Toshiichi Endo, and N. A. Jayawickrama.
